name: Solventum Corporation
sector: Healthcare / Medical devices, dental & health information systems
moat_justification: Moderate/narrow moat: category leadership in advanced wound care (V.A.C. negative-pressure therapy) and premium dental restoratives, recurring consumables, and an HIS revenue-cycle platform embedded in hospital workflows — but the measured returns do not support a wider score. Gross margin fell every year on file, from 57.7% in FY2022 to 53.5% in FY2025 (fundamentals.json), and the ROIC proxy ran 11.5% / 11.9% on a carve-out basis, dropped to 8.0% in FY2024, and prints 21.5% in FY2025 only because reported operating income contains the Purification & Filtration divestiture gain. Pricing is contested in every segment, the 3M supply agreement carries a disclosed 2027 cost step-up option, and the planned HIS separation would remove the stickiest software asset. CAP = 8.5 years.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2024, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
BASE_DIVERGENCE: latest FY OE/share -0.98 vs 3-yr median 3.99 — one of them is distorted; find out which and why
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 4.5x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
HIGH_NET_DEBT: net debt is 5.9x normalized OE — levered OE can vanish fast; stress the bear cases
one_liner: Diversified medtech spun out of 3M with leading wound/dental franchises but eroding margins and a separation-cost cash trough, moat 5/10 — at $85.81 the weighted IRR is 7.41% with IV@15% $33.24 on the normalized median base (Tier F on the TTM base); it clears 15% only below ~$33.24.
moat_for: #1 advanced wound care position (V.A.C. negative-pressure wound therapy) with recurring consumables pull-through
Premium dental restorative brands (Filtek) and orthodontic franchise with dentist familiarity / switching friction
HIS 360 Encompass revenue-cycle platform embedded in hospital coding and billing workflows — real switching costs
Regulatory-cleared portfolio, hospital channel relationships and materials IP (owned for its field of use) inherited from 3M
Diversified recurring-revenue mix: MedSurg 57.9% of FY2025 sales, HIS 16.3%, Dental 16.2% (segments.json)
moat_against: Gross margin eroded 57.7% (FY2022) to 53.5% (FY2025) — cost, mix, 3M supply markup and tariff pressure beat pricing power
Underlying ROIC proxy only 8.0% in FY2024; FY2025's 21.5% is inflated by the divestiture gain sitting in operating income
Contested everywhere: Medtronic / Smith+Nephew in wound care, Dentsply Sirona / Envista in dental, Oracle Health in HIS; pricing pressure in surgical supplies
3M long-term supply agreement: supplier holds a 2027 option to raise certain raw-material costs (disclosed ~100bp margin headwind if exercised)
Planned HIS separation removes the stickiest software asset; reported revenue CAGR on file is under 1% and growth depends on execution of the transformation plan
